title: aether_converter download job
description: Job consumed by `aether_converter download --job-file <json>`. Authoritative source: crates/aether_converter/src/download.rs (DownloadJob / SubTileSpec).

encoding.description: Elevation PNG encoding (case-insensitive). Any other value fails at runtime.

max_connections.description: Concurrent HTTP connections. Defaults to 256 when absent. The CLI download runs a fixed pool of this many requests; its window is cut 25 % per second only on >= 3 HTTP 429/503 answers in that second (floor max(max_connections / 4, 16)) and grows 10 % per clean second back to this value; timeouts, resets and slow bodies never move it (CONTRACT 9b, changelog 30). On unix, where even a raised open-file limit cannot hold 2 x max_connections + 96 descriptors, it runs (limit - 96) / 2 connections instead and says so (changelog 36). A full run also holds its output files open, one descriptor each, where they fit beside those; elsewhere each write opens its file and says so (changelog 39).

buildings_pbf_dir.description: Directory of {z}_{x}_{y}.pbf vector tiles fused onto the finished .abt tiles as a post-pass. All tiles must share one zoom level. Absent means terrain only. With buildings_pbf_ready the post-pass first waits for that marker file (changelog 45); with buildings_pbf_list only the listed tiles are read, once the list exists (changelog 51).

buildings_pbf_ready.description: File name inside buildings_pbf_dir (e.g. "_ready") whose existence declares the directory complete, so a caller can fetch the building tiles while the job downloads the terrain. With it the CLI download reads nothing in the directory before its buildings post-pass (the directory need not exist at launch); the post-pass first waits for <buildings_pbf_dir>/<buildings_pbf_ready> to exist as a file, looking at once and then every 250 ms for at most buildings_pbf_wait_s. When it has to wait it prints `[Buildings] waiting for the building tiles (<path>)` once and `[Buildings] building tiles ready after <s.s> s` when the marker appears, then burns exactly as a job whose directory was complete at launch (same .abt bytes, same `[Buildings] <n> pbf tile(s)` line). A marker still missing after buildings_pbf_wait_s fails the run (`Building tiles not ready: ...`, exit 1, its .abt files removed) - never a silent run without buildings. Write the marker last, after every tile file is complete; remove a stale one before launching. Requires buildings_pbf_dir; must be one plain file name (no / or \, not . or ..) and not a {z}_{x}_{y}.pbf/.mvt tile name, else the job fails before any request. Absent or null: unchanged (the post-pass reads the directory as it finds it). CLI download full runs only: repair jobs and the in-memory/WASM downloaders ignore it. Additive, aether_converter >= 0.2.10 (older builds ignore it and burn whatever the directory holds when their terrain is done); CONTRACT 9b, changelog 45.

buildings_pbf_wait_s.description: Seconds the buildings post-pass waits for buildings_pbf_ready - or (aether_converter >= 0.2.14, changelog 51) for the buildings_pbf_list file - counted from its first look; absent or null = 1800. Read only together with buildings_pbf_ready or buildings_pbf_list (alone it changes nothing; a repair job reads it for buildings_pbf_list only); outside 0..86400 the job fails before any request. Additive, aether_converter >= 0.2.10; CONTRACT 9b, changelog 45.

buildings_pbf_list.description: The ABSOLUTE path of a UTF-8 text file naming, one per line, the building tile files of buildings_pbf_dir the post-pass burns ({z}_{x}_{y}.pbf or .mvt, the name only; lines end in \n or \r\n; blank lines, lines starting with #, blanks around a name and a byte-order mark ignored; a name listed twice is decoded once). Only the listed files are read - buildings_pbf_dir is never listed, so it may be a store of far more tiles: the same .abt bytes, `[Buildings] <n> pbf tile(s) -> ...` line and [Tile] lines as the same job whose buildings_pbf_dir holds exactly the listed tiles. The file is the ready signal: the post-pass waits for it exactly as for buildings_pbf_ready's marker (looking at once and every 250 ms for at most buildings_pbf_wait_s; `[Buildings] waiting for the building tiles (<list path>)` / `[Buildings] building tiles ready after <s.s> s`; never coming: `Building tiles not ready: the list file <list path> (buildings_pbf_list) ...`, exit 1, the .abt files removed), then reads it once; write it last, under another name, then rename it into place. An empty list (no byte, or blank/comment lines only) burns nothing: `[Buildings] 0 pbf tile(s), no buildings in extent`. A listed tile not in buildings_pbf_dir (or unreadable) fails the run: `Building tile <name> listed in <list> is not in <dir>`, the .abt files removed. Requires buildings_pbf_dir, which must exist when the job starts; excludes buildings_pbf_ready; must be absolute - else the job fails before any request. CLI download full runs AND repair jobs (repair_source_tiles), every pass: a repair honours the list exactly as a first pass - the same checks, the listed tiles burnt onto its repaired pixels (`[Buildings] repair: ...`, the bytes of a repair over a directory of exactly those tiles), the same wait for a list that is not there and the same errors, before any file is written (its files stay unchanged on a failure); it ignores only the marker. The in-memory/WASM downloaders ignore it. Absent or null: unchanged. Additive, aether_converter >= 0.2.14 (older builds ignore it and burn the whole buildings_pbf_dir after the terrain, without waiting); CONTRACT 9b, changelog 51.

fetch_bounds.description: Optional fetch region of interest in degrees. Only source tiles intersecting it are downloaded/decoded; pixels outside keep the -9999 void sentinel. Output grid and .abt layout unchanged. Supported by the in-memory downloader only; the file-based `download` CLI rejects jobs carrying it (its sparse writer would read skipped rows as 0 m).

tile_deadline_s.description: Per-source-tile wall-clock cap in seconds across all attempts, back-offs and Retry-After waits; absent = 20 (changelog 30; was 60). At expiry the tile is a `timeout` failure and goes to the parent fill. CLI download only. Additive, aether_converter >= 0.2.6 (CONTRACT 9b, changelog 28).

repair_source_tiles.description: Source tiles [z, x, y] (z = the job's zoom) to fetch again and patch into the job's EXISTING .abt files; only output pixels wholly determined by listed tiles are rewritten, every other byte is unchanged. Each tile must intersect an output tile and every touched output file must exist, else the run fails before any request. Additive, aether_converter >= 0.2.6 (older builds ignore it and download the whole job); CONTRACT 9b 'Repair jobs', changelog 28.

cache_dir.description: Directory of the raw source-tile cache, shared by every job, service and zoom that names it, and safe for several converter processes at once. Absent, null or empty: no cache (the run is exactly as without the field). Set: every source tile is looked up in <cache_dir>/<service_key>/z<zoom>/x<x>_y<y div 256>.pack before any request (service_key = the first 16 hex digits of SHA-256(url_template, query string included, + newline + lower-cased encoding), so templates that differ only in their query never share a directory; the informational service.json records the template without its query string, so a key in the query never reaches the disk in clear text - one in the path does); a hit is decoded from the cached bytes without a request, and every HTTP 200 body that decoded and every HTTP 404 the run fetches - the parent fill's coarser tiles included - is written there. Since aether_converter 0.2.9 (changelog 40) a tile without an entry is derived without a request from the cached tiles of up to four finer zooms when they cover it (2 x 2 means in the service's encoding, stored with entry status 3; not the service's own coarser tile). Failed, timed-out, undecodable and degraded tiles are never cached. A directory that cannot be used costs one [Warn] line, never the run. CLI download only (a repair job refetches its listed tiles and rewrites their entries); the in-memory and browser downloaders ignore it. .abt bytes, every parsed line and exit codes are unchanged. Additive, aether_converter >= 0.2.8 (older builds ignore it); CONTRACT 9b 'Raw source-tile cache', changelog 38.

seam_filter.description: The seam filter. Absent, null or true: every Terrarium tile of zoom 11 or finer the CLI download decodes - fetched, read from the raw tile cache, derived from cached finer tiles, or a coarser parent of the backfill - has its mosaic-seam samples turned into voids before the parent fill, which then fills them from the coarser zooms exactly like the service's own voids (samples at or below -11000 m). A seam sample is a valid sample whose two row neighbours, or two column neighbours, are both more than 2200 m higher; a neighbour is the nearest valid sample within 2 samples inside the tile (voids skipped, never neighbours), and the rule runs again on what it voided, at most 2 passes, so a two-sample seam goes too. The cache keeps the service's bytes untouched; a tile it derives is built from filtered children (a sample void because of the seam is stored as Terrarium RGB 0,0,1 = -32767.996 m, a void to every converter). false: off - decoded exactly as aether_converter 0.2.12 decodes, for A/B runs (give them a cache_dir of their own: tiles a filtering run derived and stored hold its filtered samples). Mapbox jobs, the in-memory and the browser downloaders are never filtered. Either way stderr's [Stats] block gets `[Stats] Backfill: <n> px in <m> tile(s) filled from coarser zooms (<k> px seam samples)` (informational, changelog 49) when an arrived tile had void samples. Additive, aether_converter >= 0.2.13 (older builds ignore it and do not filter); CONTRACT 9b, changelog 49.

resolution_m.description: Metres per pixel; writer sets scale = resolution_m / 111111. XYZ samples are area-averaged over each output pixel's footprint (voids excluded from the mean); where a pixel is finer than the source zoom it takes the sample it sits in. See CONTRACT.md section 6.
